name: K-T2
description: The performance comparison of TVC and the own cloud pass (owner order 2026-11-12). Five views (ground at 200 m, inside the deck, above, orbit edge, sky from 200 m) at one universal time chosen by the field as K-T2d chooses its picks (hourly candidates from a fixed base plus a far window of 10 days; the candidate whose cover at 3 km is nearest to 0.65 and at least 0.5, with the sun 30 to 55 degrees up, the wide band 15 to 60 only where the narrow one holds none; the same in every start; each own variant then waits, with its cloud source on, until every layer draws its own map at the clock's time (at most 20 s), the TVC variant 20 s for the painter's maps; -t09DrawnCover chooses the time and the views' heading by what the clouds draw in each view instead), the same camera for every variant, the hold's stable gate (30 frames within 5 m) before each timing window, at 1707x960 and 2560x1440, Medium, A4500, vertical sync off. The definition pins what the player's settings must not decide (key 'settings', written by the runner after the profile and restored with the snapshot): raytracing Off and frame generation off (Medium's raytracing and no pacer behind the GPU frame; the interop and the ray reconstruction would be in every frame), the upscaler's quality NativeAA with qualityAuto off (the render size equals the window size, otherwise Auto renders 1707x960 in both windows; the probe emits T09.view.<name>.render_size and fails when it differs from the window), and the frame cap off (FRAMERATE_LIMIT 1000, the probe reads Application.targetFrameRate back and fails when a cap is set). Built in Release (the CPU rows are Release limits). Own starts (EVE removed, so nothing else draws clouds): off (no clouds from us: the baseline frame), plain (cloud resolution level 1), recon2 and recon3 (levels 2 and 3, one pixel of every 2x2 or 3x3 block per frame; in the views ground, inside and above only), recon4 (level 4), then at the inside view only cache (the light cache on), and cap2 (layer cap 2), and gain (cloud.sunGain and cloud.moonGain reach the pass); edge (edge-adaptive mode) and heightoff (the T13 switches off: their cost = plain minus heightoff) are not in the default list (time) and run with -atmoVariants. Output stage: the product defaults (cloud.sunUnit pi, cloud.exposure 1, cloud.outputGamma 2.2) apply with ownClouds on; the variants set cloud.sunGain only in the gain check. Noise (outside the timing window, after the pictures): for plain and recon2 to recon4 in the views ground and above the probe reads two baseline frames (no layer drawn) and two frames with the pass, each pair on consecutive frames of the held pose, and emits T09.noise.<view>.flicker (mean absolute luminance difference of the two frames in the region the pass changed), floor_flicker (the same for the baseline pair), hf (high-pass RMS, the spatial grain) and their relative forms; kt2.py divides each level by plain. Mods disabled by the runner: EVE in the own starts, Trajectories in all (96 NullReferenceExceptions a run in start 42 added CPU load that hid the GPU cost; ThroughTheEyes (FirstPerson) throws once in the space centre and stays). TVC start (EVE and Scatterer present; the probe fails the start at once without either, waits up to 60 s for the effective source Eve with a bound layer and checks EVE's renderer is Ready): tvc (cloudSource Eve, EVE draws the maps of our field), through the same views, placement, hold, stable gate and clock as the own variants, natural pictures only. The cost of the clouds in a view is the GPU frame of the variant minus the GPU frame of off at the same view and resolution (label independent; TVC against the off of the own start of the same resolution, the universal times are compared by T09.ut_spread_s), cross-checked for the own pass by the GPU profiler's group 'ReDefinition clouds' (the begin and end markers the pass puts around itself; T09.perf.markers_agree). TVC draws its own layer set (the pack's layers plus the painter's layer at 2700 m), the own pass its four layers: the columns compare two systems at the same camera, not equal clouds, and the views 'inside' (4550 m) and 'above' (8300 m) are relative to our layers, not to TVC's. tools/weather_metrics/kt2.py computes the milliseconds from the logs of all starts (the 'metrics' entry); the first TVC report's costliest labels and the labels its pattern matched are in the run's notes. Pictures: after the dwell of each view and variant (outside the timing window) the probe saves a natural picture and, for the own pass, an aid picture (the layer shader's optical-depth heat map over the scene) as t09-<start>-<view>-<variant>-<WxH>-natural.png and ...-aid-opticaldepth.png ('-half' = scaled down by two; full size for the key views of off, plain and tvc); the runner copies them to .local/work/series-pictures/K-T2 and lists them in the result; a fault of the pictures is a named warning ('Probe: warning <name>'), never a failure. A timing series, so the GPU lock is exclusive. Expected results are written in tests/series/rows/T09.json before the run. Run order: own1707 first (it validates the markers, the placement and the clock), then tvc1707.

starts.description: the own pass at 1707x960 with EVE and Trajectories removed: off, plain, recon4 in the five views, recon2 and recon3 in ground, inside and above (30 s each), then cache and cap2 at the inside view (25 s each) and the gain check; 23 windows, about 15 minutes of game time (14.8 to 15.2 minutes in the fake world at 40 to 60 frames a second, 19 minutes the limit)
TVC alone at 1707x960: the five views, 30 s each; needs EVE with the raymarched layers and Scatterer (the probe fails the start at once without them)

E40 grain against TVC (.local/plans/atmospheres/E40-grain-tvc-result.md; T09ProbeGt.cs): the own pass at 1707x960 in the views ground, inside, above and sky3 (no orbit view), 30 s each: off, plain (the product's defaults, layers.gridFine 1), and in the views ground and above full (layers.gridFine 1) and low (layers.gridFine 0.33). The GPU profiler runs with its camera markers, as in own1707 and tvc1707 (without them the first marker is the pass's own and the busy time of the off window is not the frame's work: E40 start 55): the cost is the busy difference against the off window (kt2.py). After each view's pictures the grain reading: three raw frames read one after the other, written at full size (<variant>a / b / c), rows T09.grain.<view>.tstd / blob / lap / luma / frames_apart over the view's box. About 14 minutes of scenario.

E40 grain against TVC: TVC alone at 1707x960 in the same four views with the same profiler switches and the same grain reading as gt1707 (three raw frames a / b / c per view, rows T09.grain.<view>.*); its cost is the busy difference against the off window of gt1707. Needs EVE with the raymarched layers and Scatterer.

E40 soft density, the one start of the second lead (T09ProbeSoft.cs, review .local/work/e40-soft-start59-review.md): the variants of SoftVariants (soft = the defaults, hard = layers.softDensity 0, soft32, soft100s24, up to four cost candidates) in the fair-weather scene (the K-T2d low cover, views ground and above) and at the K-T2 clock (views ground, above, inside, sky3), at 1707x960: per view the baseline (the pass running, no layer drawn), per variant three raw frames written at full size and, where the table says so, a 22 s cost window (tags fw_<variant> and k_<variant>); the sun colour line of the clouds once per scene. The variant list is fixed (plain): the table in the probe decides what runs. About 16 minutes of scenario (SoftEstimateS).

E40 start 60 (T09ProbeSoft60.cs, plan and review .local/work/e40-start60-plan-review.md and e40-start60-review.md, collector tools/weather_metrics/e40s60.py): the cost windows of soft, softr50 (the march target of before C1, all views), softcut16 (fair ground) and soft100s24 (both grounds) against TVC's four figures; the weave diagnosis (eight consecutive frames of soft, softhash and softacc05 at the fair ground, each right after four frames of its own 256-step reference); the maps the pass marches, dumped at every baseline window and type view (series-pictures/maps, tools/weather_metrics/e40c2.py --prepare-all); the extra looks (horizon, fog, rain under the deck); the views placed by the layers' type map, LAST in the clock scene (cumulus humilis, congestus, cumulonimbus, cirrus, from the ground and from above, three frames each; a type absent within 300 km is logged); the probe fails by name if the clock scene is not start 47's universal time; the light rows and the sun colour line; at 1707x960, Medium profile. The variant list is fixed (plain): the table in the probe decides what runs. About 17 minutes of plan (Soft60EstimateS 1017.5 s), about 13 minutes measured by start 59's pace.

perfNpic2560dlssqdump (a page fault, a write to an address with no resource, 4 of 6 runs, each in the first frames after a placement once the own pass was switched on) with the upscaler off (enabled False: no DLSS, whose D3D11 path runs NVIDIA's own kernels): whether the fault goes with DLSS

perfNpic2560dlssqdump with the upscaler's input scan (-redefinitionUpscalerScan): the page fault is DLSS's (own clouds and DLSS 10 of 13 runs; no upscaler 0 of 4; D3D12 off still faults), so the colour and motion vectors DLSS gets in the 90 frames after each cut are read back and their values that are not finite counted (on the D3D11 path, -redefinitionDlssD3d11, since DLSS runs on Direct3D 12)

perfNpic2560dlssqscan with the clouds' motion vectors left out of the upscaler's (variant nomv, cloud.motionVectors 0): the fault stayed 4 of 4 with DLSS's history reset at every placement, and it comes at the jump from the ground view into the cloud (the inside view) or in the pass's first frames, so whether the clouds' vectors are what DLSS faults on. The scan logs the largest motion of the 12 frames after each cut

perfNpic2560dlssqscan with FSR 3 (the mod's own compute shaders) in place of DLSS at the same render size (1707x960 of 2560x1440): the page fault came with DLSS (about 12 of 15 runs, the clouds' motion vectors off still 2 of 2) and never without an upscaler (0 of 4), which also renders at the full size. FSR at DLSS's size tells NVIDIA's code from the render size and the rig

perfNpic2560dlssqscan with DLSS's auto exposure off (-redefinitionDlssFixedExposure, autoExposure False: the fixed exposure 1): the page fault is in NVIDIA's code (DLSS about 12 of 15 runs, FSR 3 at the same size 0 of 3, DLSS's inputs finite, not negative), and the auto exposure is DLSS's part whose writes go where the picture's values say (a histogram)

perfNpic2560dlssqscan with Aftermath's call stack markers (-redefinitionGpuCrashDumpStacks: a marker with the CPU's call stack at every draw and dispatch) and its shader error reporting: the page fault in DLSS stays with the auto exposure off (3 of 3), with DLSS's four textures the same objects throughout, and never with FSR (0 of 3), so the dump has to name the call that wrote. Needs nv-aftermath-control's Global mode with resource tracking, call stacks and shader error reporting on (an administrator's command)

perfNpic2560dlssqscan with the own pass's parts taken out one at a time, each before the pass as it is in the same run (the pass's first variant faulted in about 4 of 5 runs, mostly at the jump into the cloud): here the cloud shadow (noshadow, which also writes Scatterer's ocean shadow and depth textures), then plain as the control

perfNpic2560dlssqnoshadow's design with the pass at its barest (bare: cloud.costDebug 7, no light, no shape noise, no erosion) before the pass as it is: the cloud shadow off still faulted at the jump into the cloud

perfNpic2560dlssqscan with DLSS at the full size (DLAA, quality NativeAA; the check of two thirds fails by design): the page fault came with DLSS at two thirds whatever its preset (K, M), exposure and the pass's parts (shadow off, bare), never with FSR at two thirds or without an upscaler at the full size; whether DLSS at the full size faults

the page fault comes with DLSS at any size (DLAA 2 of 2), any preset and exposure, and the own pass in any form (shadow off, bare), never with FSR or without an upscaler: the pass with all its targets and passes but no layer drawn (nolayers) before the pass as it is, to tell the clouds' content from the pass's resources
